clue.text: Mercury's counterpart, some other messenger

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mythology quiz: the Greek god who matched Rome's Mercury, another divine messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek messenger god is the equivalent of the Roman Mercury, sharing his winged sandals and role.

clue.text: Queen rings the number

definitions.note: read as 'something that numbs', an anaesthetic, not a figure

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so the Queen's letters go round the word that follows

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch encircles a figure, as if adding a ring to a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a figure but is read as numb-er, a thing that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old anaesthetic gas deadens feeling, so it is literally something that numbs a patient.

clue.text: Jerk mentions a US state

indicators.note: to jerk is to jolt sharply, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Some idiot keeps bringing up an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as a noun, a fool, but is a verb telling you to jolt the letters of MENTIONS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty states, in the American Midwest, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Island first to strike in hostile manner

indicators.note: the first letter of the word strike is what is taken

parts.note: to behave icily is to act coldly and unfriendly

explanation.surface: Islanders are the first to attack, and do so with aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean isle off the toe of Italy, an example of the definition.

clue.text: In brownish-red, a cold biscuit

indicators.note: the short pieces are placed inside the colour word

parts.note: maroon is a dark brownish-red colour
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A chilled biscuit with a reddish-brown colour, as if describing a bake.
explanation.walkthrough: A and C go in after the first letter of MAROON.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a sweet almond or coconut cookie, so it is a kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Actress having edited line, re-edit in protest

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a protest

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration through the streets

indicators.note: edited means reworked, so the letters of line and re-edit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer has a script line cut and rewritten, then rewritten again in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protest' reads as the reason for the rewrite, but it is the outer word, a street march.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was the German-born film star of The Blue Angel, so she is an example of an actress.

clue.text: Adhesive holds as window opening sideways

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the glue word goes round the small word

parts.note: cement is a glue or bonding material

explanation.surface: Glue keeps something in place, like a window that swings open to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side so it swings out like a door.

clue.text: Instrument for measuring sovereign?

definitions.meaning: a straight strip marked in inches or centimetres for gauging length
a monarch who reigns over a country; the query marks the switch of sense

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is the measuring tool somehow a monarch?
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a straight-edged measuring strip and a person who governs a realm, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory finale causing displeasure

parts.note: off means below standard, as in an off day
a finale is the ending of a show

explanation.surface: A disappointing conclusion to a story leaves the audience annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that upsets people or gives offence is causing them displeasure.

clue.text: Model iron horse, about ton, powerful beast

indicators.note: about means around, so the shaped letters surround the letter for a ton
to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new form

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A toy steam engine, an 'iron horse', weighing a ton, likened to a mighty animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' rearranges IRON HORSE into RHINOEROS, which goes 'about' C; 'ton' is a hundred, not a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhino is a huge, heavily built horned mammal, so it fits a strong animal.

clue.text: One side remaining

definitions.meaning: the opposite of right, a direction or side
still there after the rest has gone

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the port-hand side and also means leftover or still remaining after others go.

clue.text: Loyal butler set out to get European Union backing

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of butler are laid out in another order
backing means going backwards, so the two-letter abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A faithful butler departs to support the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' makes TRUEBL from BUTLER, and 'backing' turns EU into UE.
explanation.definitionFit: True-blue describes someone staunchly faithful, especially to a party or cause.

clue.text: Horse drinks in seawater

definitions.note: a noun standing for the adjective sense 'of the sea'

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the horse word swallows the small word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse gulps down sea water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word here: it is the word the mare drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine describes things found in or belonging to the sea, as in marine life.

clue.text: Repeat filling in multiple choice

indicators.note: filling means the stuffing inside, so the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to complete the repeated quiz by filling in the multiple-choice answers.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound bounced back, so to echo means to reiterate what was said.

clue.text: King almost finished eating extravagant dessert

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the shortened name goes round the next piece
almost finished means the name is cut just short of its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: Charles is the name of the current British king
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: The monarch has nearly cleared a lavish pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finished' looks like a full plate, but with 'almost' it trims the king's name by its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a pudding of fruit or cream enclosed in sponge fingers or bread, a classic dessert.

clue.text: Genius — mug following one abroad

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the mug word goes second

parts.note: ein is German for one, a foreign word for the number
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A clever person is fooled, a mug, while travelling overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a dupe but is a beer stein; EIN is German for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used for any brilliant person, so it is a byword for a genius.

clue.text: Unfortunately on trial, commercial travellers, the lot of them!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Sadly, a whole group of salesmen ends up in the dock together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges ON TRIAL into TRAINLO; 'commercial travellers' is a false phrase meaning sales reps.
explanation.definitionFit: A full train's worth of passengers is every traveller aboard, the entire lot.

clue.text: Staff machine that cuts round article on page

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the machine word goes around the short pieces

parts.note: a mower is a machine for cutting grass

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the article comes before the page letter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Workers operate a cutter going round a piece written on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the workforce available, which is what staff means as a collective noun.

clue.text: Squid caught malaria at sea!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A squid contracted a tropical fever while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid prepared as food, usually fried rings, so the words cover the same creature.

clue.text: Travel beyond a river to get legendary vessel

indicators.note: beyond means past, so the travel word comes after

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Sailing past a river mouth to reach a famous mythical ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth, so it is a legendary vessel.

clue.text: Still, lift is fast

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift means raise, so the small word is read upwards, end to start

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: The elevator has stopped and is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' and 'fast' both suggest an elevator, but one turns IS upwards to SI and the other is the season of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent means making no sound, the sense of 'still' in a still night.

clue.text: Typo, say, students recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: A misprint is reported by students who remembered it.
explanation.definitionFit: A typing error is an example of a small mistake; 'say' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Shilling in spotless little bag

indicators.note: the coin letter goes inside the word for spotless

parts.note: pure means spotless, untainted
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: An old coin rests in a pristine small pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a small pouch for carrying money, so it is a little bag.

clue.text: Figure heading for ruin, one in mess

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for a mess

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle or mess

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is on course for disaster, a person in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for ruin' reads as bound for disaster but gives just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided shape, an example of a geometric figure.

clue.text: Massive lobsters, and raw gulper eels for starters

indicators.note: starters are first courses, so the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A huge seafood platter: lobsters plus uncooked gulper eels as appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: A gulper eel is a deep-sea fish with an enormous mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means big in size, a plain synonym of massive.

clue.text: Lead sulphate's beginning to encounter dark liquid

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

parts.note: tar is a thick black liquid

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: lead sulphate starts to meet a black fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal beside 'sulphate' but means a leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film plays its leading role, so the star is the lead.

clue.text: Use marker pen here: wet biro had burst

indicators.note: a burst pen has split apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A leaking ballpoint means switching to a marker on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A wipe-clean wall panel is written on with dry-wipe markers, so it is where such pens get used.

clue.text: Study new careers with minimum of hope

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into another word
the minimum part of a word is its smallest share, the single first letter

explanation.surface: Looking into fresh jobs with barely any optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CAREERS into RESEARC, and 'minimum of hope' gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is careful investigation, so it means study as a noun or verb.

clue.text: More orderly, I had to get in line

indicators.note: to get in means to go inside, so the contraction is placed within the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row or line
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone tidier had to join a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidier is the comparative of tidy, so it means neater or more orderly.
